examples.ko: 주말에 가족과 과천에 있는 대공원에 갔어요.
examples.en: On the weekend I went to the large park in Gwacheon with my family.

examples.ko: 대공원은 걸어서 한 바퀴 도는 데 두 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes two hours to walk around the large park.

examples.ko: 이 대공원 안에 큰 동물원이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a big zoo inside this large park.

examples.ko: 대공원 입구에서 자전거를 한 시간 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I rented a bicycle for an hour at the entrance of the large park.
In spring, many flowers bloom in the large park.
You can get to the large park by subway.

explain: 대공원은 보통 이름에 붙어요. '서울대공원'처럼 공원 이름으로 쓰기도 하고, 일반 공원보다 훨씬 넓은 공원을 가리키기도 해요. 작은 동네 공원은 그냥 '공원'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 대공원 usually appears as part of a name. It can be a proper name like '서울대공원' (Seoul Grand Park), or it can point to a park much bigger than an ordinary one. A small neighborhood park is just '공원'.

examples.en: I put on lotion after washing my face.

examples.ko: 로션이 거의 떨어져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The lotion is almost gone, so I need to buy more.

examples.ko: 이 로션은 향이 은은하고 끈적이지 않아요.
examples.en: This lotion has a gentle scent and is not sticky.

examples.ko: 아기 피부는 로션으로 매일 관리해 줘요.
examples.en: I care for the baby's skin with lotion every day.
I received a bottle of lotion as a gift.
I packed both lotion and sunscreen in my bag.

explain: 얼굴 관리 제품은 '스킨', '로션', '크림'처럼 이름을 나눠 불러요. 모두 '바르다'를 써요.
explain_en: Face-care products are named separately, such as 스킨, 로션, and 크림. All of them take the verb 바르다.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 차가운 메밀국수가 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On hot days I want to eat cold buckwheat noodles.
I tried eating the buckwheat noodles with grated radish.
Buckwheat noodles are a bit coarse and nutty.
I ordered a bowl of buckwheat noodles for lunch.
After boiling the buckwheat noodles, rinse them in cold water.
This restaurant is famous for its buckwheat noodles.

explain: '막국수'도 메밀로 만든 국수라서 서로 가까운 음식이에요. 일본어 '소바'를 한국어로는 '메밀국수'라고 옮기는 경우가 많아요. 국수는 '삶다', 찬물에 '헹구다'처럼 요리 동사와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: '막국수' is also made from buckwheat, so the two dishes are close. The Japanese 'soba' is often rendered in Korean as '메밀국수'. It appears with cooking verbs such as '삶다' (boil) and '헹구다' (rinse).

examples.en: The spacecraft launch is tomorrow.
I watched the rocket launch on TV.
The launch was postponed because of the weather.
A loud sound came at the moment of launch.
The news said the satellite launch succeeded.
There are ten minutes left until launch.

explain: 주로 로켓, 우주선, 인공위성처럼 하늘로 보내는 일에 써요. '발사 성공', '발사 시간'처럼 명사끼리 이어 말하는 일이 많아요. '발사하다', '발사되다'와 같은 뿌리의 말이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for sending rockets, spacecraft and satellites into the sky. Nouns often chain with it, as in '발사 성공' and '발사 시간'. It shares a root with '발사하다' and '발사되다'.

examples.ko: 방 안에 책상을 창문 쪽으로 배치해요.
examples.en: I arrange the desk toward the window in the room.

examples.ko: 가게 입구에 의자를 두 개 배치했어요.
examples.en: We placed two chairs at the entrance of the shop.

examples.ko: 가구를 다르게 배치하면 방이 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: If you arrange the furniture differently, the room looks bigger.
They placed guides all around the airport.
The coach is thinking about where to place the players.

examples.ko: 신입 사원을 다음 달에 영업팀에 배치할 거예요.
examples.en: We will assign the new employee to the sales team next month.

explain: '놓다'나 '두다'는 그냥 놓는 일이고, '배치하다'는 어디에 둘지 생각해서 자리를 정하는 느낌이에요. 물건뿐 아니라 사람에게도 써서 '직원을 배치하다'라고 해요. 명사 '배치'는 '자리 배치', '좌석 배치'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '놓다' and '두다' just mean putting something down, while 'baechihada' implies deciding where each thing goes. It works for people too, as in '직원을 배치하다' (assign staff). The noun '배치' appears in '자리 배치' (seating plan) and '좌석 배치' (seat layout).

examples.en: Every morning I comb my hair in front of the mirror.
The puppy likes it when I brush its fur.
My hair was tangled, so I combed it for a long time.
A lot of hair came out while I was combing.
Be gentle when you brush a cat.
If you comb your hair before bed, it gets smoother.

explain: 머리를 빗는 일은 '머리를 빗다'가 더 자연스럽고, '빗질하다'는 빗으로 쓸어내리는 동작이나 동물 털을 빗어 줄 때 잘 어울려요. '빗질을 하다'처럼 '을'을 넣어 말할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: For combing hair, '머리를 빗다' sounds more natural, while '빗질하다' fits the motion of running a comb through or brushing an animal's fur. You can also say '빗질을 하다' with '을' in between.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 해마다 새해맞이 여행을 가요.
examples.en: My family goes on a New Year trip every year.
They handed out tteokguk at the New Year event.

examples.ko: 새해맞이를 위해 집 안 대청소를 했어요.
examples.en: We did a big house cleaning to welcome the new year.
We watched the sunrise at the beach to welcome the new year.
Are you all done getting ready for the new year?
I sent New Year greetings to my friends by text.

explain: 새해를 맞는 준비나 행사, 여행을 말할 때 써요. 한국에서는 새해 첫날 일출을 보러 가는 것을 '해돋이'라고 하는데, 이것도 새해맞이의 하나예요. 인사말은 '새해 복 많이 받으세요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for the preparations, events or trips for welcoming the new year. In Korea, going to watch the first sunrise of the year is called '해돋이', which is one kind of 새해맞이. The greeting is '새해 복 많이 받으세요'.

examples.en: There is a fire drill this afternoon.
A fire truck passed by with its siren on.
Every building has to get a fire safety inspection.
My uncle is a fire service worker.

examples.ko: 소방 시설이 잘 갖춰져 있어서 안심이에요.
examples.en: The fire equipment is well installed, so I feel safe.

examples.ko: 화재 때문에 소방 당국이 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The fire authorities are investigating because of the fire.

explain: '소방서', '소방관', '소방차'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 불을 끄고 막는 일과 관련된 말을 만들어요. '소방' 하나만 따로 쓰는 일은 드물고 대부분 합성어 안에서 만나요.
explain_en: It attaches in front of other words, as in '소방서' (fire station), '소방관' (firefighter), and '소방차' (fire truck), to form terms about putting out and preventing fires. It rarely stands alone and is mostly met inside compounds.

examples.en: I bumped into the door and my big toe swelled up.
My big toe hurts because of my new dress shoes.
There is a hole in the big toe part of my sock.
Try standing with your weight on your big toe.
My big toenail cracked, so I went to the hospital.
The baby plays with its big toe in its mouth.

explain: 손의 '엄지손가락'처럼 발에서 가장 굵은 발가락이에요. 가장 작은 발가락은 '새끼발가락'이라고 해요. 발가락은 '발톱', '발가락 양말'처럼 다른 말과도 붙여서 많이 써요.
explain_en: Like the '엄지손가락' on the hand, it is the thickest toe on the foot. The smallest toe is called '새끼발가락'. '발가락' also joins with other words, as in '발톱' (toenail) and '발가락 양말' (toe socks).

examples.en: The heat continued for a month.
Good things happened one after another.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 세 번 연속하여 이겼어요.
examples.en: Our team won three times in a row.
If all-night work continues, your body gets tired.
Write down consecutive numbers.
How many years in a row did the record continue?

explain: '계속하다'는 하던 일을 이어서 한다는 뜻이고, '연속하다'는 같은 일이 끊기지 않고 이어진다는 느낌이에요. '연속해서', '세 번 연속'처럼 부사 모양으로도 써요.
explain_en: '계속하다' means carrying on with something you were doing, while '연속하다' feels like the same thing following without a break. It also appears in adverb forms such as '연속해서' and '세 번 연속'.

dis.h: do something repeatedly in a row

examples.en: The baby is sleeping soundly in the stroller.
In the evening I walked in the park pushing the stroller.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터가 없어서 유모차를 들고 계단을 올랐어요.
examples.en: There was no elevator, so I carried the stroller up the stairs.

examples.ko: 유모차가 지나갈 수 있게 비켜 주세요.
examples.en: Please move aside so the stroller can pass.
I bought a stroller my friend used for cheap.
This stroller gets very small when you fold it.

explain: 한국에서는 가볍게 접히는 것을 '휴대용 유모차', 튼튼하고 큰 것을 '디럭스 유모차'라고 구분해서 불러요. 동사는 '유모차를 밀다', '유모차를 끌다'처럼 밀다·끌다를 써요.
explain_en: In Korea a light, foldable one is called a '휴대용 유모차' (portable stroller) and a sturdy, big one a '디럭스 유모차' (deluxe stroller). The verbs are 밀다 (push) and 끌다 (pull): '유모차를 밀다'.

examples.ko: 방학 동안 일과표를 직접 짜 봤어요.
examples.en: I made my own daily schedule during the vacation.
Moving by my daily schedule makes time pass well.

examples.ko: 일과표에는 점심시간이 한 시간으로 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The daily schedule says lunch is one hour.

examples.ko: 일과표가 너무 빡빡해서 쉴 틈이 없어요.
examples.en: The daily schedule is so tight that there's no time to rest.

examples.ko: 친구에게 내 일과표 좀 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: I showed my friend my daily schedule.
I put exercise time in my daily schedule too.

explain: 하루에 할 일을 시간 순서대로 적은 표예요. 학교 수업을 적은 표는 '시간표'라고 해서 달라요. 캠프나 훈련처럼 하루 일정이 정해진 곳에서도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It's a chart of what you will do during the day in time order. A chart of school classes is called '시간표', which is different. It's also commonly used for camps and training programs with a fixed daily routine.

examples.en: Before leaving, I stop at a gas station and fill up.
I filled up the tank on my way home from work.

examples.ko: 기름이 얼마 안 남아서 주유해야 해요.
examples.en: There is little fuel left, so I have to fill up.
You have to get out of the car while it is being filled.
I want to fill up on the highway, but the rest stop is far.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 주유해서 기름이 가득 차 있어요.
examples.en: I filled up this morning, so the tank is full.

explain: '주유소에서 주유하다'처럼 같은 말이 겹쳐도 자연스러워요. '기름을 넣다'라고 바꿔 말할 수 있어요. 전기차는 '주유하다'가 아니라 '충전하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Repeating the root, as in 주유소에서 주유하다, sounds fine. You can swap it with 기름을 넣다. Electric cars use 충전하다 instead of 주유하다.

examples.en: Dinner is all ready on the table.
The presentation materials are already prepared.

examples.ko: 모든 것이 다 준비되면 바로 출발해요.
examples.en: Let us leave right away once everything is ready.

examples.ko: 이불과 베개가 손님 방에 준비되어 있어요.
examples.en: Blankets and pillows are ready in the guest room.
Please call me as soon as the food is ready.
The gifts will all be ready by tomorrow.

explain: '준비하다'는 내가 하는 일이고, '준비되다'는 끝나서 갖춰진 상태예요. '준비됐어요?'는 '다 됐어요?'라는 뜻으로 일상에서 자주 물어요. '준비가 되다'로 풀어 쓰는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: '준비하다' is the act of preparing; '준비되다' is the state of being all set. '준비됐어요?' is a very common everyday question, like asking 'all set?' It is also often split up as '준비가 되다'.

dis.h: be ready; set up in advance

p.n: 마련되다 stresses that the seat was arranged or provided.

examples.en: There is a farewell party for the department head tomorrow.
At the farewell party, my colleagues gave me gifts.

examples.ko: 유학 가는 친구를 위해 환송회를 열었어요.
examples.en: We held a going-away party for our friend who is going to study abroad.
We need to book a place for the farewell party.
I'm sorry I couldn't come to the farewell party.
Like welcome parties, farewell parties are held as a work dinner.

explain: 떠나는 사람을 위해 하는 모임이에요. 새로 온 사람을 맞이하는 '환영회'와 짝으로 외우면 좋아요. 비슷한 말로 '송별회'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is a gathering held for someone who is leaving. It is good to learn it as a pair with '환영회', which welcomes a newcomer. A similar word is '송별회'.

en: flexing one's muscles; boast of one's strength

examples.ko: 형은 친구들 앞에서 힘자랑을 하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My older brother likes to show off his strength in front of his friends.

examples.ko: 힘자랑 좀 그만하고 이것 좀 같이 들어요.
examples.en: Stop showing off your strength and help me lift this.
When boys get together, they start by showing off their strength.

examples.ko: 힘자랑하느라 무거운 가방을 혼자 들다가 허리를 다쳤어요.
examples.en: He tried to show off his strength by lifting a heavy bag alone and hurt his back.

examples.ko: 그건 힘자랑이 아니라 그냥 도와주려고 한 거예요.
examples.en: That wasn't showing off, I just wanted to help.

examples.ko: 동네 씨름 대회는 마을 사람들의 힘자랑 무대예요.
examples.en: The neighborhood wrestling contest is a stage for villagers to show their strength.

explain: 힘이 센 것을 뽐내는 모습을 말하고, '힘자랑하다'라고도 해요. 조금 놀리거나 장난스럽게 말할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It describes showing off how strong one is, and you can also say '힘자랑하다'. It is often used in a slightly teasing or playful tone.
